title: sparse
summary: Create sparse matrices from full arrays, sizes, or row/column/value triplets.

gpu_support.notes: Sparse matrices are host-resident CSC values. GPU inputs are gathered before construction because RunMat's acceleration API currently exposes dense tensor handles.

description: `sparse` creates a sparse matrix. RunMat stores sparse matrices in compressed sparse column form and supports the common MATLAB construction forms: conversion from a full array, empty sparse allocation by size, and triplet assembly from row indices, column indices, and values.
behaviors: `sparse(A)` converts a full single, double, or logical array to sparse storage, storing only nonzero values. Logical inputs retain logical class with the CSC pattern as the authoritative set of true elements. Exact integer arrays are accepted only in `runmat` compatibility mode and retain their integer class.
`sparse(m, n)` returns an `m x n` sparse double matrix with zero stored entries.
`sparse(i, j, v)` creates a sparse matrix whose size is inferred from the largest row and column subscripts.
`sparse(i, j, v, m, n)` creates an `m x n` sparse matrix and errors if any subscript falls outside those dimensions.
`sparse(i, j, v, m, n, nzmax)` accepts the MATLAB allocation hint for compatibility; RunMat's storage is still sized from the produced nonzero entries.

Duplicate numeric `(i, j)` entries are summed and entries whose final value is zero are not stored. Duplicate logical triplets combine by logical OR and false values are not stored. RunMat-extension integer triplet values are summed in their exact integer class.
Row and column subscripts are one-based positive integers. If either subscript input uses an integer datatype, both must use the same integer datatype.

Sparse matrices support scalar row/column indexing and linear indexing; scalar selections return sparse `1 x 1` values, unstored entries read as zero, and linear indices are resolved in column-major order.
Sparse slice indexing preserves sparse storage for non-scalar selections.
Sparse indexed reads and assignments preserve CSC storage and the sparse value class. Typed sparse integer reads and assignments are available only in `runmat` compatibility mode.

Sparse real matrices interoperate with `+`, `-`, and `.*` for sparse-sparse, sparse-dense, dense-sparse, sparse-scalar, character, logical, and complex operands. Addition and subtraction with dense, complex, or nonzero scalar operands return full storage when unstored sparse zeros become nonzero; sparse-preserving real products and sparse-sparse sums/differences return sparse storage.

examples.output: `A` is sparse-scaled then densified by `full`; `B` is a full matrix because sparse zeros become twos.

faqs.question: Which sparse construction forms are supported?
faqs.answer: RunMat supports `sparse(A)`, `sparse(m,n)`, `sparse(i,j,v)`, `sparse(i,j,v,m,n)`, and `sparse(i,j,v,m,n,nzmax)` for real single, double, and logical data. Exact integer payloads are a mode-gated extension available only when compatibility is set to `runmat`.

faqs.question: Does RunMat store sparse matrices densely?
faqs.answer: No. The runtime uses compressed sparse column storage with column pointers and row indices plus class-native stored numeric values. Sparse logical matrices need no parallel value payload because each stored CSC position is true.

faqs.question: What happens to duplicate triplets?
faqs.answer: Duplicate numeric row/column pairs are summed; duplicate logical values combine with `any`, matching MATLAB sparse assembly semantics.

faqs.question: Can sparse matrices live on the GPU?
faqs.answer: Not yet. If you pass a `gpuArray` to `sparse`, RunMat gathers it and builds a host sparse matrix. Native GPU sparse handles can be added once the acceleration API grows sparse storage.

faqs.question: Can sparse matrices store integer values?
faqs.answer: MATLAB-compatible modes reject sparse integer construction, casts, restoration, indexed access or assignment, and sparse-integer operation results. `runmat` mode exposes exact signed and unsigned sparse integer storage as a deliberate extension.

faqs.question: Which operations interoperate with sparse matrices today?
faqs.answer: Core introspection such as `size`, `numel`, `class`, `whos`, `nnz`, `find`, scalar and slice indexing, real and complex `+`, `-`, and `.*` interop, transpose, and conjugate transpose understand sparse values. Broader sparse linear algebra will build on this representation.

faqs.question: Can sparse matrices be assigned through indexing?
faqs.answer: Yes. Scalar, linear, and planned slice assignment preserve sparse storage and the target sparse class while removing entries assigned the class-appropriate zero or false value.

gpu_residency: Sparse values are currently host-resident. Passing a GPU tensor to `sparse` triggers a gather, after which RunMat builds a compressed sparse column matrix on the host.
gpu_behavior: The GPU metadata for `sparse` is intentionally marked as gather-immediate. This makes the representation transition explicit to the planner and prevents pretending that dense GPU buffers are native sparse matrices.
